summary: Well-motivated, preregistered experimental study of prompt-injection against an agentic NetOps prototype with thorough artifact recording. The preregistered design and published artifact-hashes are strong; however important methodological, reporting, and reproducibility gaps remain and the presented confirmatory evidence does not yet justify the paper's interpretation without clarifications and additional analyses.
critical_issues: Planned vs analyzed sample discrepancy not fully explained in the manuscript: preregistration planned 160 paired units but analysis reports 150 complete pairs and 10 unavailable pairs—the paper must report which preregistered pairs were excluded, exact causes (infrastructure vs parser vs contamination), and demonstrate adherence to the preregistered missingness/stopping rules.

Key experimental artifacts required to verify claims are described as published in the bundle but the manuscript omits concrete, inspectable examples: (a) exact model identifiers (full API model/version strings) and the deterministic prompt templates used for each condition; (b) representative adversarial payloads from the attack corpus; (c) representative raw LLM outputs that were parsed to CLI ASTs; (d) example parsed ASTs and the deterministic parser code or canonical parsing rules. Without these, neither vulnerability nor defense failure can be audited.

Insufficient description of the validator and RAG/provenance enforcement: the paper asserts a deterministic runtime validator and provenance-based grounding but gives no machine-verifiable specification of the validator predicates (logic/rules), the RAG index construction procedure and index hash, or the exact runtime checks that caused an action to be accepted or rejected. This is central to the claim that the particular defense did not reduce attack-success.

Statistical interpretation is weak for the preregistered estimand and power plan: the preregistration targeted a large (≥70%) relative reduction and a paired design; the report provides a McNemar p=0.25 and a bootstrap CI including zero but does not (a) reconcile realized power given the 150 pairs, (b) recompute minimum detectable effect under observed baseline rate (~0.98), or (c) present exact paired contingency table rows and decision thresholds used by the exact test. The manuscript should present these items explicitly and re-evaluate confirmatory claims accordingly.

Construct-validity concern: baseline attack-success at ~98% (and guarded success at 100%) suggests the adversarial corpus may be near-trivial for the studied pipeline or that parser/acceptance criteria are permissive. The paper does not analyze attack difficulty, nor provide per-attack-type breakdowns to show whether results generalize across attack classes (obfuscation, indirect-instruction, instruction-masking).

Reproducibility metadata gap: execution manifest reports only 163 model_calls_used for ~300 completed episodes—this ratio and heavy use of call-cache entries are plausible but unexplained in the text. The manuscript must explain the caching strategy, per-run model-call counts, and show how deterministic caching did not bias outcomes (e.g., by masking variability or reflighting results).
required_revisions: Add a concise audit appendix (or inline machine-readable supplement) that includes: exact model identifiers (API strings/versions), the frozen deterministic prompt templates for each condition, and the parser invocation commands; provide artifact paths and hashes already recorded so reviewers can inspect exact inputs/outputs without ambiguity.

Publish in the manuscript (or supplement) representative examples from the attack corpus, corresponding raw LLM outputs (baseline and guarded), the deterministic parser output (canonical CLI AST), and the simulator verdicts (accepted/rejected) for at least 10 illustrative paired runs covering different task clusters and attack types.

Provide a formal, machine-verifiable description of the deterministic runtime validator predicates (logic/rules), the sandbox behavior, and the RAG index construction (how sources were filtered, proof of index hash used at runtime). Explain precisely how provenance was checked and how provenance failures lead to exclusions or rejections.

Report a full paired contingency table (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00) for the preregistered primary contrast in the main paper (not only in artifacts), and (a) recompute realized power and the minimum detectable relative reduction given the observed baseline rate and the 150 pairs; (b) report exact McNemar inputs and confirm the exact test implementation; (c) provide bootstrap code and seeds used to produce CIs.

Explain all excluded/failed episodes in a compact table: list task ids excluded, reason (infrastructure, parser failure, contamination, other), timestamps, and whether retries were attempted per preregistered policy. If any post-preregistration changes to exclusion rules or reruns occurred, disclose and justify them explicitly.

Provide stratified exploratory summaries required by the preregistration: per-attack-type success rates, per-task-cluster summaries, false-block (benign-correct config rejected) rates for each defense, and per-model-family breakdown. If some exploratory contrasts were omitted from analysis because of missingness, state that and show sensitivity analyses (worst/best-case imputations) as preregistered.
optional_revisions: If space permits, add short example pseudo-code for the validator predicates to help readers judge practical correctness of the defense design.

Add a brief qualitative analysis of why the implemented validator failed to reduce attack-success (e.g., which classes of adversarial instructions it did not capture), using representative failing examples.
Run and report a small robustness check on at least one additional model/version or on a strengthened validator predicate to demonstrate whether outcomes are implementation-specific or general.
Include a short table explaining caching behavior and per-run model-call counts to help other researchers budget replication efforts.
